own_solution.law: Maxwell speed distribution: fraction with speed > v is erfc(x) + (2/sqrt(pi)) x exp(-x^2), x = v/v_p, v_p = sqrt(2kT/m); amount = n * fraction

notes: m = 6.6471e-27 kg; 2kT/m = 1.24655e6 m^2/s^2; v_p = 1116.5 m/s; x = 1.79133, x^2 = 3.20886; erfc(x) = 0.011288; (2/sqrt(pi)) x e^{-x^2} = 0.081667; fraction 0.092955; amount 0.04648 mol. At 317 K: x^2 = 3.03677, x = 1.74263; erfc = 0.013722; second term 0.094365; fraction 0.108087; amount 0.05404 mol. Pressure: for fixed n and T the pressure only fixes the (unstated) volume and does not enter the speed distribution, so I class it C (it would equally be defensible as not entering at all). 62 kPa is well within the ideal-gas regime. Pressure variants T5A1D/T3034 differ only in wording; 17 K variants consistent; 'modest amount' sentences carry no number (numeral-free). The atomic mass unit value is not stated but is a standard constant.
